prerequisites.title: X developer account
prerequisites.detail: Sign in at console.x.com with an X account, accept the Developer Agreement and Policy, and describe how you will use the API.

prerequisites.title: Credits for API usage
prerequisites.detail: Buy credits upfront in the Developer Console. Requests are blocked if the balance goes negative or a spending limit is reached.

prerequisites.title: X representative contact
prerequisites.detail: Ads API access beyond your current permissions requires reaching out to an X representative.

steps.title: Create developer account and app
steps.detail: Sign in at console.x.com, accept the agreement, describe your use case, and create a new app.
steps.done_when: The app exists in the Developer Console.

steps.title: Draft use-case description
steps.detail: Write a specific use-case text that matches your access needs, since vague descriptions are reported as a common rejection reason.
steps.done_when: Text is ready to paste into the console.

steps.title: Save client ID and secret
steps.detail: Copy the OAuth 2.0 Client ID and Secret immediately; they are shown only once.

steps.title: Copy Composio redirect URI
steps.detail: Copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard and add it as a callback URL in the X app settings.
steps.done_when: Callback URL is saved in the X app.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create a custom auth config through Composio's API using your client ID and secret.

steps.title: Buy credits
steps.detail: Purchase credits in the Developer Console and optionally set a spending limit.

steps.title: Contact X representative
steps.detail: Ask your X representative for Standard Access for the Ads API.

traps.title: Credentials are shown only once
traps.detail: If you lose them you must regenerate, which invalidates the old ones.

traps.title: Requests stop when credits run out
traps.detail: Requests are blocked at your spending limit or if the balance goes negative.

traps.title: Pay-per-usage plans have a read cap
traps.detail: They are capped at 3 million Post reads per monthly billing cycle; more needs an Enterprise plan.

traps.title: Use-case changes need approval
traps.detail: A substantive change to your use case requires notifying X and getting approval first.

traps.title: Callback URLs must be pre-registered
traps.detail: Any callback URL must be configured in the app settings, and HTTPS is required for OAuth steps.

traps.title: Rate limit 429 errors
traps.detail: Exceeding per-user or per-app limits returns 429 until the window resets.

blockers.what_it_means: A third-party blog reports rejections usually come from a vague use case or a request that does not match the tier; this is not documented X policy.
blockers.what_to_do: Resubmit with a specific, accurate use-case description.
Wait for the window to reset and reduce call frequency.

open_questions: Does X require any review before outside users can authorize a production app? The docs found state none; confirm with X developer support.
How long does Standard Access for the Ads API take? Ask your X representative.
Do OAuth 2.0 user tokens expire and need refresh handling in production? Check the X OAuth 2.0 docs.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: To use this method, you'll need a Bearer Token, which you can generate by passing your API Key and Secret through the
evidence.answer: A Bearer Token can alternatively be generated by passing the API Key and API Secret through the POST oauth2/token endpoint.

evidence.quote: click where it says "revoke" next to the Bearer Token in the "keys and tokens" section of your App settings.
evidence.answer: A Bearer Token can be revoked with the POST oauth2/invalidate_token endpoint, or by clicking "revoke" next to the token in the Keys and tokens section of the App settings.

evidence.question: G4

evidence.question: G4

evidence.answer: The x_auth_access_type parameter overrides the access level an application requests for a user's account.

evidence.answer: The end user is sent to the oauth/authorize step in a web browser to authorize the app. The page does not mention a customer admin approval step.

evidence.answer: X requires HTTPS for all OAuth authorization steps.

evidence.answer: Any callback URL used with the request_token endpoint must be configured in the app's settings on developer.x.com.

evidence.question: G10

evidence.question: G10

evidence.answer: Callback URLs are registered in the app's settings on developer.x.com.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: The X API uses **pay-per-usage** pricing. No subscriptions—pay only for what you use.
evidence.answer: The X API uses pay-per-usage pricing with no subscriptions; you pay only for what you use.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: Purchase credits upfront in the Developer Console. Credits are deducted as you make API requests.
evidence.answer: Credits are purchased upfront in the Developer Console and are deducted as API requests are made.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: No contracts, subscriptions, or minimum spend. Start and stop anytime.
evidence.answer: The X API has no contracts, subscriptions, or minimum spend, and you can start and stop anytime.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: All prices are per resource fetched (reads) or per request (writes/actions).
evidence.answer: X API reads are charged per resource fetched and writes or actions are charged per request.

evidence.quote: Pay-per-usage plans are capped at **3 million Post reads per monthly billing cycle**. If you need higher volume, upgrade to an [Enterprise plan](/forms/enterprise-api-interest).
evidence.answer: Pay-per-usage X API plans are capped at 3 million Post reads per monthly billing cycle; higher volume requires an Enterprise plan.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: These endpoints are priced at **\$0.001 per resource** (1,000 resources for \$1).
evidence.answer: For the Owned Reads case (your own developer app reading your own data), endpoints are priced at $0.001 per resource.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: Prices are subject to change. Current rates are always available in the [Developer Console](https://console.x.com) and on the [developer.x.com pricing page](https://developer.x.com/#pricing).
evidence.answer: X API prices are subject to change; current rates are published in the Developer Console and on the developer.x.com pricing page.

evidence.question: G7

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: It is possible for an account credit balance to go slightly negative. In this case, API requests will be blocked until you add credits to cover the negative balance.
evidence.answer: If the account credit balance goes negative, X API requests are blocked until credits cover the negative balance.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: To receive free xAI credits, you must link your xAI team to your X developer account.
evidence.answer: To receive free xAI API credits earned from X API purchases, the developer must link their xAI team to their X developer account.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: This list covers only toolkits that support OAuth.
evidence.answer: This page does not list an app called X. X does not appear in either the Composio-managed table or the bring-your-own table, so nothing here is specific to X.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Composio can provide the OAuth app that your users authorize when they connect a toolkit. You do not need to register an OAuth app or supply its client ID and client secret.
evidence.answer: In general (not specific to X), Composio can supply the OAuth app, so the developer does not need to register one or supply a client ID and secret.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: If the field does not contain that method, register your own OAuth app and supply its client ID and client secret.
evidence.answer: To check whether a toolkit gets a Composio-managed OAuth app, read composio_managed_auth_schemes from the toolkit endpoint. If the OAuth method is not in that field, you must register your own OAuth app and supply its client ID and client secret.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Some toolkits support more than one authentication method. A toolkit appears under **Composio-managed OAuth available** when Composio manages at least one OAuth method. Open the toolkit page to check each method.
evidence.answer: Some toolkits support more than one authentication method, and a toolkit can be Composio-managed for at least one OAuth method while you must check each method on its toolkit page.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: If your application is limited to any of the below app-level permissions and you wish to access additional endpoints, please reach out to your X representative to apply for **Standard Access**.
evidence.answer: To access endpoints beyond the listed app-level permissions, the developer must reach out to an X representative to apply for Standard Access. The page does not say this step is required before outside customers can connect.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Developers who requested Ads API access prior to July 2023 may have requested any of the following app-level permissions, which are now included with the Standard Access level:
evidence.answer: For the Ads API, developers who requested access before July 2023 may have had Analytics (read-only), Campaign Management & Creative (read & write), Custom Audiences (read & write), or Conversion (read & write) app-level permissions, which are now included in Standard Access.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: User cannot access Campaign Management, Creative or Custom Audiences endpoints, but will be able to pull metrics by passing through creative entities in the request parameters of the Analytics endpoints.
evidence.answer: The Analytics (read-only) permission does not allow access to Campaign Management, Creative, or Custom Audiences endpoints, but metrics can be pulled by passing creative entities in Analytics request parameters.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: To pull the granularity of media\_id or media\_name, the user application would need to have Ads API write access.
evidence.answer: Pulling media_id or media_name granularity from Analytics requires Ads API write access.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: User also has access to Analytics endpoints.
evidence.answer: The Campaign Management & Creative (read & write) permission also grants access to Analytics endpoints.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: User also has access to Campaign Management, Creative, and Analytics endpoints.
evidence.answer: The Custom Audiences (read & write) permission also grants access to Campaign Management, Creative, and Analytics endpoints.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: User may or may not have access to other Ads API endpoints.
evidence.answer: The Conversion (read & write) permission covers Mobile and Web Conversion endpoints and may or may not include other Ads API endpoints.

evidence.quote: Developers who requested Ads API access prior to July 2023 may have a limit of 5 user OAuth tokens on their application.
evidence.answer: Developers who requested Ads API access before July 2023 may be limited to 5 user OAuth tokens per application.

evidence.answer: To raise the user OAuth token limit, the developer must reach out to an X representative.

evidence.answer: X does not increase rate limits for any Ads API endpoint.

evidence.answer: In your own OAuth app's settings, the authorized redirect URI should be set to your own endpoint.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Users will see "Composio wants to access your account" during OAuth.
evidence.answer: With a managed app, users see 'Composio wants to access your account' during OAuth, which is fine for internal tools, prototypes, and development.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: In production, users should see your app name, not "Composio."
evidence.answer: In production, users should see your app name rather than 'Composio', which is the most common reason to switch to your own app.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Composio requests sensible defaults for each toolkit.
evidence.answer: Managed apps request Composio's sensible default scopes for each toolkit, and those defaults may not include everything you need.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Composio's default scopes may not include everything you need (e.g., write access to a specific Google API).
evidence.answer: Composio's default scopes may not include everything needed, for example write access to a specific Google API, which is a reason to use your own app.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Managed apps share quota across all Composio users.
evidence.answer: Managed apps share their rate-limit quota across all Composio users.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Your own app gets a dedicated quota.
evidence.answer: Your own app gets a dedicated quota, which is a reason to use a custom app when you are hitting rate limits.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum polling interval; your own app can use shorter polling intervals where supported.
evidence.answer: Managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum polling interval for triggers; your own app can use shorter polling intervals where supported.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Self-hosted or regional variants (e.g., a private Salesforce subdomain) need their own OAuth app.
evidence.answer: Self-hosted or regional variants, such as a private Salesforce subdomain, need their own OAuth app rather than the managed one.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: To check whether Composio provides the OAuth app for a toolkit, see [Managed OAuth apps](/toolkits/managed-auth).
evidence.answer: To check whether Composio provides the OAuth app for a given toolkit, consult the Managed OAuth apps page.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: You can still create a custom auth config for branding, scopes, rate limits, polling intervals, or custom instances.
evidence.answer: You can still create a custom auth config for branding, scopes, rate limits, polling intervals, or custom instances even when a managed app exists.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Use your own credentials for toolkits where users see consent screens (GitHub, Google, Slack) and Composio managed auth for the rest.
evidence.answer: You can choose per toolkit: use your own credentials where users see consent screens (GitHub, Google, Slack) and managed auth for the rest, with each toolkit getting its own auth config.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Review rejects listings that are not a real X API product, and listings that pretend to be someone else.
evidence.answer: This review covers only the public Developer Exhibit listing (name, logo, screenshots, website, content), not the gate that lets outside customers connect an app; it checks listing authenticity and content, and it is not an identity or security review.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: How long: varies from immediate to several days. There's no published SLA and no queue position to check.
evidence.answer: Per a third-party blog (SocialAPI, a competitor selling a read-only X data API, so treat as commercial and unverified), X developer-portal approval was reported as taking anywhere from immediate to several days, with no published SLA.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: Usually a vague use-case description, or a request that doesn't match the tier.
evidence.answer: The same blog reports that rejections are usually due to a vague use-case description or a request that doesn't match the access tier; this is an unverified general claim, not a documented X policy.

evidence.question: G6
evidence.quote: You must notify us of any substantive modification to your use case and receive approval before you may begin using X Content for that new purpose.
evidence.answer: Reviews repeat on changes: a substantive change to the approved use case requires notifying X and receiving approval before the new use starts. No published review timeline or yearly re-review was found on this page.
